title: The Recipe of Maple Street
premise: Rafael Dunmore has survived four schools in six years by staying invisible, but Maplewood High sits on the site of a demolished orphanage, and when her junior English teacher assigns a college essay on 'a place that made you,' Rafael's research uncovers a 1974 fire the school board erased from every record. With help from Marisol Vega, a local girl whose grandmother survived the fire, and a failing archive of buried documents, Rafael traces how the town's founding families covered up the deaths of nine children to protect their own names. As the school board moves to demolish the last surviving wing before homecoming, Rafael must choose between her safe, anonymous life and publishing the truth. The book ends at the school board's emergency meeting, where Rafael reads the recovered names aloud; the demolition is halted, a memorial is commissioned, and Rafael finally writes an essay about herself — not as the new kid, but as someone who belongs.
about_author: Ines Nystrom grew up in a mill town in upstate New York where half the buildings had stories nobody would tell. She writes young adult fiction about quiet kids who find loud truths.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. First day at Maplewood High; she maps exits, memorizes social hierarchies, and perfects invisibility. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: English teacher Mr. Okafor assigns the college essay: 'Describe a place that shaped you.' Rafael freezes — she has no place. Beat: quiet panic beneath a blank page.

chapters.title: Basement Smell
chapters.summary: Rafael notices the school's west wing smells of smoke after rain. A janitor, Gus, tells her not to ask about it. Beat: first crack in the ordinary.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: POV shift to Marisol Vega, who works the library desk and watches Rafael copy old yearbooks. She leaves a note: 'You're looking for 1974.' Beat: wary curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Didn't Print
chapters.summary: Rafael finds the 1974 yearbook pages razored out. The library catalog shows a gap. Beat: the thrill of a real mystery replacing essay dread.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her grandmother Elena goes silent whenever the school is mentioned; a burned-edge photograph falls from a recipe box. Beat: inherited grief.

chapters.title: Nine Empty Desks
chapters.summary: Rafael learns the west wing was once St. Brigid's Home for Children, closed after 'the incident.' Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Essay That Isn't
chapters.summary: Okafor conferences with Rafael about her empty draft; she almost tells him, then deflects. Beat: fear of being seen versus need to be seen.

chapters.title: Board Minutes
chapters.summary: At town hall, Rafael requests 1974 school board minutes; the clerk says they're 'lost in a flood.' Beat: first evidence of deliberate erasure.

chapters.title: Elena Speaks Sideways
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Over empanadas, Elena describes the orphanage's garden without saying why she was there. Beat: tenderness wrapped around trauma.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Rafael discovers three current board members descend from the families who owned the land. Beat: the conspiracy gains faces.

chapters.title: Detention with Gus
chapters.summary: Gus reveals he's kept a key to the sealed wing for thirty years because 'somebody should remember.' Beat: reluctant ally found.

chapters.title: Inside the West Wing
chapters.summary: Rafael and Marisol break in at night: scorched doorframes, children's initials carved in a closet. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Elena's recipe box contains a handwritten list of nine names, each with a birthday. Beat: the dead become specific.

chapters.title: Homecoming Pressure
chapters.summary: The board announces the west wing will be demolished before homecoming for a new gym. Beat: a ticking clock starts.

chapters.title: Rafael Almost Transfers
chapters.summary: Her mother proposes moving again for work; Rafael, for the first time, wants to stay. Beat: belonging becomes a stake.

chapters.title: Newspaper Girl
chapters.summary: Student journalist Priya offers the school paper — if Rafael can prove it. Beat: hope with strings attached.

chapters.title: The Fire Marshal's Report
chapters.summary: A state archive yields a report: the fire was arson, never prosecuted. Beat: outrage ignites.

chapters.title: Whose Name Was On It
chapters.summary: The arson suspect's initials match Aldous Merrick, now the board chairman's grandfather. Beat: personal villainy revealed.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Rafael and Marisol are caught leaving the wing by security; their parents are called. Beat: consequences crash down.

chapters.title: Grounded and Determined
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV under house arrest; she transcribes everything into her college essay draft, which has become the real story. Beat: purpose through punishment.

chapters.title: Elena's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Shown the name list, Elena finally speaks: she was the tenth child, the one who got out. Beat: catharsis and weight.

chapters.title: Merrick's Offer
chapters.summary: Chairman Merrick privately offers Rafael a scholarship letter of recommendation if she drops it. Beat: temptation, and contempt for it.

chapters.title: Priya Pulls Back
chapters.summary: Priya's advisor kills the story under pressure from the district. Beat: allies falter; isolation deepens.

chapters.title: The Flood That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rafael proves the 'flooded' minutes were destroyed two years after the fire, on Merrick family letterhead. Beat: smoking gun.

chapters.title: Okafor Reads It
chapters.summary: Rafael submits her essay — the true one. Okafor reads it silently, then says, 'This needs an audience bigger than me.' Beat: adult validation.

chapters.title: Vandalized
chapters.summary: Someone trashes Rafael's locker and steals her notes. Beat: fear, and confirmation she's close.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the List
chapters.summary: From memory, Elena rewrites all nine names and dates; Marisol records her testimony on video. Beat: memory as resistance.

chapters.title: The Gymnasium Rally
chapters.summary: Homecoming week; the school celebrates the new gym while Rafael distributes photocopied flyers. Beat: defiance in public.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: A friend from student council sells out the location of Elena's video testimony to Merrick. Beat: trust shattered.

chapters.title: Stolen Testimony
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The video drive vanishes; Elena wavers, ready to give up. Beat: despair at its lowest.

chapters.title: Backup
chapters.summary: Rafael reveals she uploaded everything to the cloud weeks ago — a habit from being the new kid everywhere. Beat: her outsider skills become her strength.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting Notice
chapters.summary: Public comment opens at Thursday's emergency demolition vote. Three days. Beat: the clock's final turn.

chapters.title: Practice
chapters.summary: In Okafor's classroom, Rafael reads her speech aloud until her voice stops shaking. Beat: courage rehearsed.

chapters.title: Thursday Night
chapters.summary: The packed meeting; Merrick dismisses 'gossip,' then Rafael takes the mic and reads the nine names aloud. Beat: climax begins.

chapters.title: Elena Stands
chapters.summary: Elena rises, identifies herself as a survivor, and the room turns; a councilwoman demands the vote be tabled. Beat: the buried are witnessed.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Demolition halted 5–2; an independent investigation ordered; Merrick resigns under the lights. Beat: victory, earned not given.

chapters.title: Memorial Garden
chapters.summary: Weeks later, ground is broken for a memorial garden where the wing stood; the nine names go on a bronze plaque. Beat: grief given a home.

chapters.title: The Essay
chapters.summary: Rafael finishes her college essay about Maple Street — about choosing a place instead of fleeing one. Beat: identity claimed.

chapters.title: Enrolled
chapters.summary: Senior year begins; Rafael's locker stays shut, but she eats lunch with Marisol, Priya, and Gus in the sun. Beat: belonging, at last.
